title: Physics-guided discovery of dynamical dark-energy equations of state through iterative AI reasoning
summary: Phenomenological model building has traditionally relied on human reasoning: equations are proposed from theoretical intuition, analogy, or empirical convenience, and only then tested against data. Here we show that this cycle can be recast as an iterative AI reasoning process for dynamical dark energy. Our framework uses a large language model to propose equations of state together with cosmological rationales, grounded by retrieval from the dark-energy literature and refined through autonomous evaluation. Each candidate is embedded in a cosmological model, optimized against observations, and assessed using likelihood performance and theoretical consistency. An independent language-model critic scores the physical motivation, novelty, clarity, stability and implementation validity of both the equation and its rationale, allowing subsequent proposals to evolve jointly in mathematical structure and physical reasoning. Applied to cosmological data combinations including supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations and Planck likelihoods, the framework identifies two parameterizations that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been explored and that are competitive with established forms. For Pantheon+ supernovae, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and the full Planck 2018 temperature, polarization, and lensing likelihoods, the best AI-selected model attains larger Bayesian evidence than the traditional parameterizations considered here by more than one unit. These results show that AI-guided reasoning can complement physical model building by proposing and evaluating interpretable phenomenological parameterizations for dynamical dark energy.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that large language models can autonomously generate and evaluate novel, interpretable models for dynamical dark energy, outperforming traditional parameterizations on key cosmological datasets.
AI.motivation: Phenomenological model building for dynamical dark energy traditionally depends on human intuition and empirical convenience, motivating the need for an automated AI framework to improve and accelerate this process.
AI.method: The paper employs a large language model to iteratively propose and refine equations of state coupled with cosmological rationales, using dark-energy literature for grounding and autonomous evaluation through embedding in cosmological models, optimization against observations, and scoring by an independent language-model critic.
AI.result: The AI framework identifies two novel phenomenological parameterizations for dynamical dark energy competitive with established models, with one achieving higher Bayesian evidence on combined cosmological datasets including Pantheon+ supernovae, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and Planck 2018 likelihoods.
AI.conclusion: AI-guided iterative reasoning effectively complements traditional physical model building by autonomously generating and evaluating interpretable and physically motivated parameterizations for dynamical dark energy, advancing phenomenological model construction.

title: Cooling, conduction, compact objects: Gravothermal evolution of dissipative self-interacting dark matter halos
comment: 19 pages, 16 figures, 2 tables; to be submitted to A&A
summary: Many proposed self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models give rise to radiative processes that can dissipate energy. Understanding their impact on astrophysical objects through simulations and comparing the results with observations may thus constrain SIDM models. In this work, we systematically investigate how dissipation alters the gravothermal evolution of isolated SIDM halos by independently varying dissipation and heat conduction and identify potential observational signatures. To this end, we present the first extension of the $N$-body formalism for frequent small-angle self-interactions (fSIDM) to include effective dissipation. We compare all results for isolated halos with a dissipative gravothermal fluid model to assess its validity and limitations. We find that dissipation qualitatively changes the gravothermal evolution of SIDM halos beyond simply accelerating collapse. Sufficiently strong central cooling can invert the usual role of heat conduction: the formation of an isothermal core is suppressed such that conduction remains directed inward throughout the evolution. Outer halo regions beyond the scale radius can cool efficiently rather than being heated by conduction, resulting in a larger region of mass infall and a less pronounced indentation between the core and the outer halo in the final density profile. These effects depend strongly on the cooling rate but are comparatively insensitive to the angular dependence of the self-interaction cross section. We further show that weakly dissipative self-interactions can explain the properties of the recently observed strong lens perturber in JVAS~B1938+666 with significantly shorter evolution times or, equivalently, smaller cross sections compared to the elastic case. Our results open a new route to connecting halo structure and recently reported compact objects to dark-sector microphysics.

AI.tldr: This work extends SIDM simulations to include dissipation, showing that it drastically alters halo evolution and can explain certain observed astrophysical phenomena, thereby connecting dark matter microphysics to halo structures and compact objects.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of radiative dissipation processes in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) models on astrophysical objects and to constrain these models through simulations and observations.
AI.method: Development and application of the first extension of the N-body formalism for frequent small-angle SIDM with effective dissipation; systematic variation of dissipation and heat conduction parameters; comparison with a dissipative gravothermal fluid model for isolated halos.
AI.result: Dissipation qualitatively changes gravothermal evolution beyond accelerating collapse, suppressing isothermal core formation and maintaining inward heat conduction; efficient cooling in outer halo regions alters mass infall and density profile features; effects depend strongly on cooling rate but weakly on angular dependence of self-interactions; weakly dissipative SIDM can explain observed lens perturber properties with shorter evolution times or smaller cross sections than elastic SIDM.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating dissipation in SIDM models reveals new dynamics in halo evolution, offering novel observational signatures and a link between halo structure, compact objects, and dark-sector microphysics, potentially advancing constraints on SIDM theories.

title: BayeSN $\times$ Dovekie: Joint Photometric Cross-calibration and SED Modelling of Type Ia Supernovae
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present a new framework for BayeSN, the hierarchical Bayesian SED model for type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), incorporating cross-calibration of samples observed across heterogeneous telescopes. This framework is the first to parametrise the filter wavelength and zero-point offsets commonly used in SN~Ia cosmology within SN SED model training, enabling additional constraint on cross-calibration from SNe beyond the standard stellar-based cross-calibration pipeline. We apply this framework to train a new G26 BayeSN model on the same SED model training sample used in recent cosmological analyses, an order-of-magnitude increase over previous BayeSN training samples, and include a novel training methodology to leverage high-redshift SNe Ia in BayeSN training. We present the G26 model and apply it to the DES-SN5YR sample to assess performance, finding a 12 per cent reduction in $σ_{\rm NMAD}$ scatter when compared with SALT3.Dovekie; 0.164 mag compared with 0.185 mag for a sample of likely SNe Ia at $z < 0.7$, without bias corrections. We additionally present constraints on cross-calibration wavelength and zero-point shifts from our framework when using the latest `Dovekie' calibration constraints as a prior. This work is a key step towards a full end-to-end cosmological analysis with BayeSN; the new G26 model is incorporated within the public BayeSN code.

AI.tldr: A novel hierarchical Bayesian framework for the BayeSN SED model integrates cross-calibration parameters, enabling training on a larger diverse SN Ia sample including high-redshift data. The resulting G26 model improves brightness scatter measurements and calibration constraints, enhancing cosmological analysis accuracy.
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy and reliability of type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) cosmological analyses by addressing cross-calibration challenges across heterogeneous telescopes in spectral energy distribution (SED) modeling.
AI.method: Developed a new hierarchical Bayesian framework extending the BayeSN model that parameterizes filter wavelength and zero-point offsets during SED training, incorporating a large training sample including high-redshift SNe Ia and leveraging prior calibration constraints.
AI.result: The new G26 BayeSN model trained on an expanded dataset reduces scatter in brightness measurements by 12% compared to the SALT3.Dovekie model, improves cross-calibration parameter constraints, and is implemented publicly for cosmological applications.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating cross-calibration directly within the BayeSN SED training framework leads to more precise SN Ia distance estimates and is a significant advancement toward end-to-end cosmological analysis using BayeSN.

title: Testing X-ray selection effects with four rich, yet X--ray--faint, galaxy clusters
summary: A robust understanding of selection effects in galaxy cluster studies is crucial for both astrophysical and cosmological applications. Examining clusters identified through different observational strategies, even in small numbers, helps to illuminate potential biases inherent to each method. We selected four rich galaxy clusters in the Northern Hemisphere whose early Swift X-ray Telescope (XRT) observations indicated unusually low central X-ray emission, making them unlikely to be detected in X-ray surveys. Spectroscopic follow-up confirms that all four systems are genuine galaxy clusters, rather than projections of multiple clusters or groups along the line of sight. Their optical richness, estimated using one of the baseline Euclid cluster richness estimators, implies masses of $\log M_{200}/M_\odot \sim 14.6$ and independently confirms the absence of additional massive structures along the line of sight. Deep XRT follow-up reveals highly disturbed X-ray morphologies: three clusters exhibit at least two distinct X-ray peaks, while the remaining cluster has an axis ratio exceeding 1.5. Spectroscopy shows that galaxies associated with different parts share the same redshift, demonstrating that these substructures are physically connected rather than chance projections. These clusters display low central X-ray surface brightness and total X-ray luminosities suppressed by roughly one dex for their richness, making them undetectable in X-ray surveys as eROSITA. We estimate $\sim$20\% as a lower limit for the poorly sampled population, albeit based on a small sample. Our results demonstrate that even rich clusters in the northern $z<0.3$ Universe can be missed by X-ray selection and that the X-ray variety captured by X-ray surveys underestimates the true cluster diversity.

AI.tldr: Four optically rich galaxy clusters with unusually low X-ray emission were confirmed and shown to be physically connected but highly disturbed, revealing that X-ray surveys miss a substantial population of such clusters, affecting cluster census and selection biases.
AI.motivation: To understand selection effects and biases in galaxy cluster surveys by examining clusters missed in X-ray observations.
AI.method: Selected four rich galaxy clusters with low central X-ray emission from Swift XRT data, confirmed cluster nature with spectroscopy, estimated masses from optical richness, and conducted deep follow-up X-ray and spectroscopic observations.
AI.result: Confirmed these clusters are genuine and highly disturbed with suppressed X-ray luminosities, making them undetectable by standard X-ray surveys like eROSITA; estimated that such clusters represent at least 20% of the population.
AI.conclusion: X-ray selection methods miss a significant fraction of rich galaxy clusters due to their disturbed morphologies and low central X-ray brightness, underestimating cluster diversity and impacting astrophysical and cosmological studies.

title: Scintillation of the first-known pulsar planetary system
summary: We present a scintillation study of the first-known pulsar planetary system, PSR~B1257+12, using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). A total of 31 observations with durations greater than or equal to 30 minutes were analyzed. For 14 longer observations (greater than or equal to 120 minutes), one-dimensional autocorrelation function analyses yielded the scintillation timescale, scintillation bandwidth, and frequency-drift rate for 12 epochs. Two observations show strong periodic modulation in the frequency-domain auto-correlation function, likely caused by astronomical-unit-scale structures along the propagation path, preventing reliable measurements of the scintillation timescale and bandwidth. In three observations, secondary spectra reveal simultaneous detections of inner, middle, and outer arcs. Analysis of the annual modulation of the inner-arc curvature indicates isotropic scattering, with a screen distance of $233\pm28$~pc and transverse velocity $V_{\rm scr,α}=-7.16\pm2.16$ km~s$^{-1}$, $V_{\rm scr,δ}=-41.07\pm5.69$ km~s$^{-1}$. Delay-profile analysis for both the inner and outer arcs suggest spectral exponents consistent with, or smaller than, the Kolmogorov value. Under isotropic scattering, the screen--pulsar distances are $354\pm22$~pc and $166\pm12$~pc for the middle and outer arcs. Combining the results from long-term timing analyses with our scintillation measurements, we find that the dispersion measure (DM) variations are primarily dominated by plasma located further away from the pulsar. The low DM-change rate of the outer arc and the absence of nearby scattering screens suggest that the immediate environment of the pulsar may be relatively clean. Alternatively, scattering screens closer to the pulsar may exist but remain undetected, requiring higher-sensitivity or longer-duration observations.

AI.tldr: Using FAST observations of pulsar PSR B1257+12, the study characterizes scintillation properties revealing multiple scattering screens and isotropic scattering. Dispersion measure variations imply plasma is mainly located far from the pulsar, indicating a relatively clean immediate environment or the presence of undetected closer scattering screens.
AI.motivation: To investigate the scintillation properties of the pulsar planetary system PSR B1257+12 using high-sensitivity radio observations, addressing the plasma environment and scattering properties along the propagation path.
AI.method: Analysis of 31 FAST radio telescope observations, employing one-dimensional autocorrelation functions for scintillation timescale, bandwidth, and frequency-drift rate measurements; secondary spectral analysis to detect scattering arcs; annual modulation modeling to determine scattering screen properties; delay-profile analysis to evaluate spectral exponents.
AI.result: Identification of isotropic scattering with screen distance ~233 pc and specific transverse velocities; simultaneous detection of multiple scattering arcs indicating multiple scattering screens at different distances; dispersion measure variations dominated by plasma farther from the pulsar, suggesting a relatively clean local environment around the pulsar or undetected closer screens.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals complex scattering structures along the line of sight to PSR B1257+12, with isotropic scattering and multiple scattering screens. The pulsar's immediate environment appears relatively clean based on low DM-change rates, but further sensitive observations are needed to detect possible nearby scattering screens.

title: The impact of evolving cosmic filaments on mass and spin evolution of dark matter halos
summary: The evolution of galaxies is closely tied to that of their host dark matter halos, which is in turn strongly modulated by the surrounding large-scale environment. Cosmic filaments are expected to influence the peculiar motions, mass assembly and angular momentum of nearby halos through highly anisotropic matter flows. In order to fully capture the dynamic interplay between the filaments and halos, we develop an algorithm to trace the progenitors of individual filaments identified at z=0 with DisPerSE in a cosmological N-body simulation, by quantifying the spatial similarity between a descendant filament and progenitor candidates. This enables us to reconstruct filament-by-filament evolutionary histories, including their bulk drift and the evolution of density profiles, from which splashback radii and core overdensities are derived. Using these time-dependent properties, we re-examine halo phase-space trajectories in a filament-centric frame that evolves with time. This eliminates biases inherent to static models by separating halo motions from the motion of the filaments, allowing trajectories to be identified more reliably. We find that as halos approach high-density filaments, their mass accretion rates are systematically suppressed beginning at the filament outskirts, suggestive of tidal stripping or suppressed net accretion. Furthermore, the evolution of halo spin alignments exhibits a clear departure from stochastic random-walk expectations. This suggests that distinct mass flow regimes in and around filaments exert different torques on infalling halos, thereby changing their angular momentum. Our findings, derived from a sample screened for major mergers, highlight the pure dynamical impact of the filamentary environment. Ultimately, we demonstrate that tracking the simultaneous co-evolution of filaments and halos is essential for accurately characterizing environmental effects.

AI.tldr: A dynamic algorithm tracing filament progenitors reveals that cosmic filaments suppress halo mass accretion and alter spin alignments through anisotropic tidal torques, emphasizing the need to study filament-halo co-evolution to understand environmental impacts on galaxy formation.
AI.motivation: Investigate the dynamic interplay between cosmic filaments and dark matter halos to better understand their co-evolution and environmental effects on halo properties.
AI.method: Develop an algorithm to trace progenitors of filaments identified at z=0 in cosmological N-body simulations using spatial similarity metrics, allowing reconstruction of filament evolutionary histories and analysis of halo phase-space trajectories in a filament-centric, time-evolving frame.
AI.result: Found that halos experience suppressed mass accretion rates near filament outskirts, indicative of tidal stripping or reduced accretion, and observed non-random evolution of halo spin alignments caused by different torque regimes in filament environments.
AI.conclusion: Tracking the co-evolution of filaments and halos in a dynamic framework is crucial for accurately characterizing environmental influences on halo mass assembly and angular momentum evolution, beyond static models and merger-driven effects.

title: Evidence for protostellar jets as a population of hadronic gamma-ray sources
summary: Stars are born in darkness, deep within cold, dense molecular clouds where gravity drives the collapse of gas and dust, giving rise to protostars, the earliest stages of stellar evolution. Once considered purely thermal sources, these young systems are now emerging as sites of energetic non-thermal activity. While radio synchrotron jets hinted at the presence of relativistic electrons, direct confirmation of proton acceleration remained elusive. Here we report a statistically significant detection of gamma rays from a population of young stellar objects, revealing a Galactic class of Gamma-Loud Protostars. Observations point towards particle acceleration within protostellar jets, where gamma-ray emission arises from protons interacting with surrounding molecular clouds via pion decay. We find a correlation between cosmic-ray output and bolometric luminosity, suggesting that particle acceleration scales with the system's mechanical power. These findings open a new observational window into the role of non-thermal processes in protostellar evolution and suggest that gamma-ray studies of protostars can provide critical insights into accretion, ejection, and feedback in star formation. This previously overlooked emission traces the energetic feedback that young stars inject into their surroundings, shaping the conditions for subsequent star and planet formation.

AI.tldr: This study reveals that young protostars emit gamma rays due to proton acceleration in jets, establishing a new class of Gamma-Loud Protostars and highlighting their role in energetic feedback during star formation.
AI.motivation: To explore and confirm the presence of non-thermal energetic processes, specifically proton acceleration, in young stellar objects (protostars), which had previously been considered primarily thermal sources.
AI.method: Statistically significant detection of gamma rays from a population of young stellar objects using gamma-ray observations; correlation analysis between cosmic-ray output and bolometric luminosity was performed to understand the scaling of particle acceleration.
AI.result: Discovery of Gamma-Loud Protostars as a Galactic class; identification that gamma-ray emission arises from proton interactions with molecular clouds via pion decay within protostellar jets; demonstrated a correlation between cosmic-ray output and mechanical power of the system.
AI.conclusion: Young protostars are confirmed as sites of energetic non-thermal activity with proton acceleration, providing new insight into their energetic feedback through gamma-ray emission; this opens new avenues to study accretion, ejection, and feedback mechanisms influencing star and planet formation.

title: A self-consistent analytical model for both the photoionization rate and reionization history
comment: 22 pages, 8 figures (main text) + 4 pages (appendices). Prepared for submission to JCAP. Comments welcome!
summary: Recent developments at the intersection of cosmology and astrophysics have highlighted the need for improved analytical models of observables that probe the Epoch of Reionization. With few exceptions, fast analytical treatments of reionization suitable for use in Bayesian inference have been limited to modeling the reionization history, $x_i(z)$. Such models cannot take full advantage of observables that constrain $x_i$ indirectly. One such observable is the photoionization rate of neutral hydrogen, $Γ_{\rm HI}(z)$, which can be inferred from the mean transmission of the Lyman-$α$ forest of high-redshift quasars and galaxies. It has been shown by several prior works that the evolution of $Γ_{\rm HI}$ at $5 \lesssim z \lesssim 6$ is highly sensitive to the tail end of reionization, potentially providing a tight astrophysical constraint on the reionization timeline. We present a new analytical formalism, based on the cosmological radiative transfer equation, that self-consistently predicts $x_i$ and $Γ_{\rm HI}$. We test our model against detailed radiative transfer simulations and find it to be percent-level accurate in $x_i$ and $20-30\%$ accurate in $Γ_{\rm HI}$ at $z \lesssim 6$ - better than or comparable to existing observational uncertainties. Finally, we demonstrate that modest shifts in the ionizing photon output of high-redshift galaxies and/or the endpoint of reionization lead to differences in $Γ_{\rm HI}$ much larger that the model's intrinsic uncertainty, highlighting its utility for interpreting existing data. We explore the origin of modeling uncertainty in $Γ_{\rm HI}$ and comment on future pathways for improvement.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an improved analytical model using cosmological radiative transfer to predict the ionization history and hydrogen photoionization rates during the Epoch of Reionization, achieving high accuracy suitable for interpreting observational data.
AI.motivation: To develop improved analytical models that can accurately predict observables indirectly constraining the Epoch of Reionization, specifically targeting the photoionization rate of neutral hydrogen, which current models inadequately address.
AI.method: A new analytical formalism based on the cosmological radiative transfer equation was developed to self-consistently predict both the ionization history $x_i$ and the photoionization rate $\Gamma_{\rm HI}$.
AI.result: The model achieves percent-level accuracy in predicting $x_i$ and 20-30% accuracy in $\Gamma_{\rm HI}$ at redshifts less than 6, performing comparably or better than existing observational uncertainties. It also shows sensitivity to variations in the ionizing photon output and reionization endpoint beyond intrinsic model error.
AI.conclusion: The presented analytical model provides a robust framework for interpreting photoionization rates from high-redshift observations, improving constraints on the reionization timeline. Future improvements can further reduce modeling uncertainties in $\Gamma_{\rm HI}$.

title: Damping of Fast Radio Bursts in the Inner Magnetospheres of Magnetars
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, submitted to the Astrophysical Journal Letters
summary: We investigate the propagation of fast radio bursts (FRBs) through magnetar magnetospheres. Previous work showed that, in the inner magnetosphere, GHz radio waves propagate as fast magnetosonic waves and undergo resonant three-wave interactions that transfer their energy into trapped Alfvén waves. Using three-dimensional force-free electrodynamics simulations, we demonstrate that FRBs would excite Alfvénic fluctuations, leading to strong nonlinear attenuation of the radio signal. In quiescent dipolar magnetospheres, the nonlinear decay stays efficient within $\sim10$--$100$ magnetar radii; charge starvation of the excited Alfvén waves stops the decay at larger radii. For FRBs propagating within relativistic magnetic outflows launched during magnetospheric eruptions, three-wave interactions remain efficient and constrain the escape radius to $\gtrsim10^2$--$10^3$ magnetar radii for luminous bursts. Our results confirm that nonlinear plasma processes strongly limit the escape of FRBs from the inner magnetospheres of magnetars.

AI.tldr: This study uses 3D simulations to show that nonlinear interactions in magnetar magnetospheres significantly attenuate FRBs, limiting their escape radius to tens or hundreds of magnetar radii depending on the magnetospheric conditions.
AI.motivation: To understand how fast radio bursts (FRBs) propagate through magnetar magnetospheres and how plasma processes affect their escape and attenuation.
AI.method: Three-dimensional force-free electrodynamics simulations to model the propagation of GHz radio waves and their interaction with Alfvén waves via resonant three-wave interactions in magnetar magnetospheres.
AI.result: FRBs excite Alfvénic fluctuations that cause strong nonlinear attenuation of the radio signal; nonlinear decay is efficient within 10–100 magnetar radii in quiescent magnetospheres and extends to larger radii (≥100–1000 magnetar radii) in relativistic magnetic outflows, limiting the escape of FRBs from the inner magnetospheres.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear plasma processes, specifically three-wave interactions involving fast magnetosonic and Alfvén waves, strongly restrict the ability of FRBs to escape from the inner magnetospheres of magnetars, imposing constraints on the escape radius that depend on the magnetospheric environment.

title: Validation of the Hybrid Bias Expansion model for the galaxy bispectrum
summary: The Hybrid Bias Expansion model (also known as Hybrid Effective Field Theory, HEFT) provides a promising way to extend the range of validity of perturbative large-scale structure modelling by replacing perturbative gravitational evolution with the nonlinear displacement field measured from $N$-body simulations. While this approach has already been shown to improve the modelling of the power spectrum, its validity at the bispectrum level has not yet been established. In this work we perform a first systematic real-space validation of the Hybrid bispectrum model using DESI-like LRG and ELG mock catalogues constructed at fixed cosmology on volumes similar to those of DESI's LRG samples. We find that the model remains self-consistent up to $k_{\rm max}^B \simeq 0.25\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, while clear signs of breakdown appear for a similar EFT tree-level bispectrum approach at $k_{\rm max}^B \gtrsim 0.13\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We also show that adding matter cross-statistics significantly improves the precision of the recovered bias parameters, while a partial third-order extension including only the $δ^3$ operator does not extend the validity range. Finally, we find a strong hierarchy among the bispectrum basis terms when grouped by total bias-operator order, with the lowest-order sectors dominating the total amplitude, which has important implications in emulation strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper validates the Hybrid Bias Expansion model for bispectrum analysis using DESI mock data, showing it surpasses EFT approaches in accuracy and range. Inclusion of matter cross-statistics helps parameter recovery, while higher-order terms offer limited improvement. The dominance of low-order bias terms has implications for future modeling strategies.
AI.motivation: To validate the Hybrid Bias Expansion model (HEFT) at the bispectrum level, extending its success beyond power spectrum modeling for large-scale structure.
AI.method: Performed systematic real-space validation of the Hybrid bispectrum model using DESI-like LRG and ELG mock catalogues at fixed cosmology and realistic volumes, comparing model performance against EFT-based approaches.
AI.result: The Hybrid bispectrum model is accurate up to k_max^B ≈ 0.25 h Mpc^-1, outperforming EFT tree-level approaches which break down beyond k_max^B ≈ 0.13 h Mpc^-1. Inclusion of matter cross-statistics improves bias parameter estimation. Partial third-order extensions do not extend validity. Dominance of lowest-order bias sectors was identified.
AI.conclusion: The Hybrid Bias Expansion model provides a more extended validity range at the bispectrum level compared to traditional EFT approaches and offers improved bias parameter recovery when using matter cross-statistics. However, higher-order operator extensions do not necessarily increase model validity, and the hierarchical structure of bispectrum terms should inform emulation methods.

title: Nonlinear Decay of Fast Magnetosonic Waves through Weak Turbulence: Force-Free Electrodynamics Simulations
comment: 22 pages, 9 figures, submitted to The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We investigate the propagation of low-frequency fast-magnetosonic (FMS) waves in highly magnetized environments. Such conditions are relevant to the escape of GHz fast radio bursts potentially produced in the inner magnetospheres of magnetars. It remains an open question whether such waves can escape without substantial reprocessing. Using relativistic force-free electrodynamics simulations, we confirm the key theoretical predictions of Golbraikh & Lyubarsky (2023) and demonstrate that FMS waves undergo efficient nonlinear conversion into secondary FMS and Alfvén waves via the parametric decay instability. This process continues to drain energy from the primary FMS waves even after approximate energy equipartition between the FMS and Alfvén components is established. The resulting spectrum of excited waves is broad, extending across much of the inertial range in $k$-space within the simulation domain. Our results indicate that FMS waves likely do not escape magnetar magnetospheres without substantial dissipation and spectral broadening.

AI.tldr: Simulations show that low-frequency fast-magnetosonic waves in magnetar magnetospheres undergo nonlinear decay into other wave modes, preventing their escape without substantial energy loss and spectral spreading.
AI.motivation: To understand whether low-frequency fast-magnetosonic (FMS) waves can escape highly magnetized magnetar magnetospheres without significant alteration, given their relevance to GHz fast radio bursts.
AI.method: Relativistic force-free electrodynamics simulations were employed to study the propagation and nonlinear interactions of FMS waves in highly magnetized environments.
AI.result: FMS waves undergo efficient nonlinear parametric decay instability, converting into secondary FMS and Alfvén waves, leading to energy drain from primary waves and broad spectral excitation. This indicates substantial dissipation and spectral broadening preventing their escape.
AI.conclusion: Low-frequency FMS waves likely cannot escape magnetar magnetospheres without experiencing significant nonlinear reprocessing, dissipation, and spectral broadening, impacting the understanding of fast radio burst propagation.

title: Fireworks at Cosmic Dawn: relieving BAO-CMB tensions with the Pop III.1 Flash
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to ApJL, comments welcome
summary: A Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) optical depth of $τ\sim 0.09$, several $σ$ in excess of the latest Planck low-$\ell$ EE polarization measurement, has been proposed as a way to reconcile the preference for a sub-minimal neutrino mass sum in a combined analysis with CMB and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) three-year data. Reionization, however, is not just probed by $τ$. It is also constrained by Ly$α$ forest observations that indicate a late end of reionization, and the patchy kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (pkSZ) effect which prefers a short duration. We explore whether an early phase of reionization can achieve a high $τ$ while remaining consistent with both Ly$α$ forest and pkSZ constraints. As a concrete example, we consider supermassive Pop III.1 stars, dark-matter-powered metal-free stars proposed as progenitors of supermassive black holes. Within this framework, self-regulating ionizing feedback imposes a minimum source separation of $\sim 1 \, \text{cMpc}$, consequently limiting large-scale ionization fluctuations and reducing the pkSZ power on observationally relevant scales. Our fiducial model realizes an optical depth of $τ= 0.087$ with a Pop III.1-driven flash ionization phase centered at $z = 20$, while evading the most conservative $2σ$ upper limits on the pkSZ signal from the most recent South Pole Telescope data release. More broadly, our findings motivate further exploration of early reionization models with weakly clustered sources as a possible resolution of tensions between BAO and CMB measurements.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an early reionization phase driven by supermassive Pop III.1 stars to explain a high CMB optical depth ($\tau \sim 0.09$), while satisfying constraints from Ly$\alpha$ forest and pkSZ observations. This model helps reconcile discrepancies in neutrino mass constraints derived from combined CMB and DESI data.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by the tension between a high optical depth $\tau \sim 0.09$ inferred from some combined CMB and DESI data analyses and the lower values from Planck low-$\ell$ EE polarization measurements, along with constraints from Ly$\alpha$ forest and pkSZ effect observations on reionization history.
AI.method: The authors explore a concrete early reionization scenario involving supermassive Population III.1 stars, which are dark-matter-powered metal-free stars. They model self-regulating ionizing feedback that enforces a minimum separation between sources, reducing large-scale ionization fluctuations and pkSZ power. They analyze the resulting reionization history and its compatibility with observational pkSZ limits from the South Pole Telescope and Ly$\alpha$ forest.
AI.result: Their fiducial model achieves an optical depth of $\tau = 0.087$ with a Pop III.1-driven early ionization flash centered at redshift $z=20$. This scenario remains consistent with conservative $2\sigma$ upper limits on pkSZ power and late reionization constraints from Ly$\alpha$ forest data. It suggests that an early, weakly clustered reionization phase can reconcile optical depth values with multiple observational probes.
AI.conclusion: Early reionization models involving weakly clustered sources like supermassive Pop III.1 stars provide a viable pathway to attain high CMB optical depth $\tau$ while remaining consistent with Ly$\alpha$ forest and pkSZ constraints. This approach offers a promising potential resolution to tensions between BAO and CMB measurements related to neutrino mass inference.

title: Short-Range Forces Can Catalyze Extreme Orbital Evolution in Hierarchical Triples
summary: Hierarchical triples are promising environments for producing exotica such as black hole mergers and hot Jupiters, because of the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (ZLK) effect, whereby a distant tertiary can torque an inner binary to high eccentricity over secular timescales. In the double-averaged (DA) approximation to ZLK, this eccentricity excitation is suppressed by apsidal precession due to `short-range forces' (SRFs) like relativity and tidal/rotational bulges. Here we show that, when the DA approximation is relaxed, SRFs often catalyze, rather than suppress, extreme eccentricity behavior. This occurs because SRFs can drive large, discrete jumps in the binary's effective `adiabatic invariants' during high-eccentricity episodes. These nonadiabatic jumps can dramatically alter the maximum/minimum eccentricity and secular period of astrophysically relevant triples, including some for which SRFs were previously thought irrelevant. Even the angular momentum component $j_z$ evolves secularly -- to our knowledge, this is the first time such evolution has been demonstrated from a quadrupole-order, three-body mechanism. In short, binaries may explore much more of phase space than is implied by any (semi-)analytic ZLK theory of which we are aware. We demonstrate this at the test-particle quadrupole level; in a companion paper we show how even more-extreme behavior occurs when the jumps are combined with octupolar ZLK evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that short-range forces, previously believed to suppress eccentricity excitation in hierarchical triples, actually enhance it by causing nonadiabatic jumps when the double-averaged approximation is relaxed, leading to more diverse and extreme orbital dynamics.
AI.motivation: To investigate how short-range forces (SRFs) affect eccentricity excitation in hierarchical triple systems beyond the double-averaged (DA) approximation of the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (ZLK) effect.
AI.method: Relax the DA approximation and analyze the impact of SRFs on the evolution of hierarchical triples at the test-particle quadrupole level, showing how SRFs induce large, discrete jumps in the binary's effective adiabatic invariants during high-eccentricity episodes.
AI.result: SRFs can catalyze extreme eccentricity behavior by driving nonadiabatic jumps that significantly alter maximum/minimum eccentricity and secular period, causing secular evolution of the angular momentum component $j_z$. This expands the phase space explored by binaries beyond predictions from existing (semi-)analytic ZLK theories.
AI.conclusion: Relaxing the DA approximation reveals that SRFs play a critical role in enhancing eccentricity excitation in hierarchical triples, enabling more extreme dynamical behavior than previously understood, with implications for astrophysical phenomena such as black hole mergers and hot Jupiters.

title: Statistical Field Theory for Weak Gravitational Lensing
comment: 30 pages, 17 figures. Prepared for submission to PRD. A companion paper introducing the sft-wick formalism and package is submitted at the same time. Comments welcome
summary: Standard weak-lensing calculations treat lensing as a linear remapping of the matter field along the line of sight. We instead formulate lensing as a stochastic field theory for the Sachs optical scalars, driven by random Ricci-focusing and Weyl-shearing fields. The resulting path integral generates a diagrammatic expansion for arbitrary $n$-point correlation functions of lensing observables, organised into linear response, nonlinear propagation, and driving-field cumulants. The conventional calculation emerges as the lowest-order, linear-propagation limit. Beyond it, nonlinear Sachs evolution couples to driving-field non-Gaussianity, mixing the matter cumulant hierarchy into the lensing hierarchy. A selection rule governs the couplings: an $n$-point observable receives a direct contribution from the $n$-point driving-field cumulant, and its leading hierarchy-mixing correction from the $(n+1)$-point cumulant via one nonlinear Sachs interaction, with higher cumulants entering only at higher order. The two-point function, for instance, is corrected by squeezed three-point cumulants of Ricci focusing and Weyl shearing, letting small-scale modes source larger scales and feeding the lensing $E$- and $B$-modes equally. Rather than a restrictive approximation scheme, the formalism is a paradigm shift: a unified framework naturally accommodating path corrections, higher-order matter statistics, stochasticity, and small-scale effects.

AI.tldr: This work reformulates weak-lensing as a stochastic field theory for Sachs optical scalars, enabling a unified and systematic treatment of nonlinear, stochastic, and higher-order statistical effects beyond the traditional linear approximation.
AI.motivation: Conventional weak-lensing calculations rely on linear remapping of the matter field, which restricts the treatment of nonlinear effects, higher-order statistics, and stochasticity in lensing observables.
AI.method: The approach uses a path integral formulation generating a diagrammatic expansion for n-point correlation functions of lensing observables, organized into linear response, nonlinear propagation, and driving-field cumulants. It derives selection rules governing cumulant interactions and incorporates non-Gaussian driving-field statistics.
AI.result: The framework recovers conventional calculations as a lowest-order limit and reveals how nonlinear Sachs evolution couples with driving-field non-Gaussianity, mixing matter cumulants into the lensing hierarchy. It predicts corrections to the two-point function from squeezed three-point cumulants, enabling small-scale modes to influence larger scales and affecting both lensing E- and B-modes equally.
AI.conclusion: This paper presents a new paradigm for weak-lensing calculations by formulating lensing as a stochastic field theory of Sachs optical scalars, moving beyond the conventional linear remapping approach to accommodate nonlinear and stochastic effects.

title: On the Contribution of Local Sources to the Galactic Cosmic-Ray Spectrum: An Exact Series Solution for Two-Zone Diffusion
comment: submitted to PRD, The code accompanying this paper will be released soon
summary: Measurements of cosmic-ray proton and helium spectra below the knee show deviations from simple power laws, including multi-TeV structures. A possible explanation is that one or a few nearby sources contribute an additional component to the local spectrum. However, previous study shows that a dominant local contribution is statistically unlikely under a homogeneous diffusion model. In this work, we investigate how this probability changes if cosmic rays experience inefficient transport near their sources, motivated by observations of extended gamma-ray emission around Galactic accelerators. We derive a series Green's function that enables fast calculation of the particle distribution in this scenario, making Monte Carlo calculations for Galactic source populations feasible. The inner slow-diffusion region delays escape and redistributes the arriving particles in time and energy. In Monte Carlo realizations, the probability that the strongest local source becomes comparable to the background at $10\,\rm{TeV}$ increases from about $0.4\%$ in homogeneous diffusion to $1.7$--$2.2\%$ in the two-zone models. Thus inhibited near-source transport weakens, but does not remove, the statistical difficulty. We then examine cataloged nearby candidate supernova remnants and show that a $10\,\rm{TeV}$ feature can be reproduced only with additional assumptions, especially a harder local injection spectrum and a favorable diffusion coefficient. The predicted contribution of a given source changes strongly among different particle transport model. Therefore, the local source interpretations are plausible but highly model dependent, and require independent constraints on source injection history, particle transport mechanisms, and local interstellar turbulence.

AI.tldr: This study shows that inefficient cosmic-ray transport near sources increases the probability of local sources influencing cosmic-ray spectra at 10 TeV, but the interpretation remains model-dependent and requires additional constraints.
AI.motivation: To understand the deviations from simple power laws in cosmic-ray proton and helium spectra below the knee, particularly the multi-TeV structures, and to explore the role of a local source contribution under more realistic diffusion conditions motivated by gamma-ray observations.
AI.method: Developed a two-zone diffusion model incorporating inefficient transport near cosmic-ray sources, derived a series Green's function for rapid particle distribution calculations, and performed Monte Carlo simulations of Galactic source populations to evaluate the probability of local source dominance at 10 TeV.
AI.result: The probability of a dominant local source at 10 TeV increases from 0.4% under homogeneous diffusion to 1.7-2.2% in the two-zone model with near-source slow diffusion, indicating inhibited transport weakens but does not eliminate statistical challenges. Catalogued nearby supernova remnants can reproduce observed features only with additional assumptions (harder local injection spectrum, favorable diffusion coefficients), highlighting strong model dependence.
AI.conclusion: Near-source slow diffusion increases the likelihood of a local cosmic-ray source contributing significantly to observed spectra, but statistical challenges remain. Local source interpretations are plausible yet highly sensitive to assumptions about injection spectra, transport mechanisms, and interstellar turbulence, necessitating further independent constraints.

title: Reheating as a variational probe of cosmological observables
summary: We formulate reheating as a constrained variational problem in the space of equation-of-state histories, rather than attempting to describe it through microscopic models. We introduce a regularized functional framework that identifies reheating histories which extremize a given cosmological observable under minimal physical assumptions. As illustrative applications, we consider prompt gravitational waves, induced gravitational waves, and primordial black holes. We find that different observables select qualitatively different regions of reheating-history space. These examples demonstrate that cosmological observables define distinct extremal directions in reheating-history space and can therefore be used to systematically explore the space of post-inflationary expansion histories.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a variational approach to characterize reheating after inflation by extremizing cosmological observables in equation-of-state history space, showing that different observables highlight distinct reheating scenarios, enabling systematic analysis of the post-inflationary universe.
AI.motivation: To explore reheating after inflation without relying on complex microscopic models, enabling a systematic investigation of post-inflationary expansion histories.
AI.method: Formulated reheating as a constrained variational problem in the space of equation-of-state histories, introducing a regularized functional framework to find reheating histories that extremize cosmological observables under minimal physical assumptions.
AI.result: Demonstrated that different cosmological observables select distinct extremal regions in reheating-history space, illustrated with applications to prompt gravitational waves, induced gravitational waves, and primordial black holes.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological observables define unique extremal directions in the space of reheating histories, facilitating systematic exploration of post-inflationary expansion without detailed microscopic modeling.

title: On the braking index evolution of PSR B0540-69: wind braking of pulsars
summary: The pulsar PSR B0450-69 has both a braking index measurement and spin-down state change. After its spin-down state change, it shows an increasing braking index with time. Previously, it is pointed out that the spin-down state change may be caused by an enhanced particle wind. The prediction is that its braking index in the high spin-down state will be smaller. The current measured braking index is approaching the previous prediction. The transient variation of braking index may be due to a small varying part of the particle number density. The final braking index evolution is found to be in an exponential form. The braking index of PSR B0540-69 is expected to approach some steady value. Future braking index measurement may make clear the physics for the braking index evolution. It may also help to make test different particle acceleration potential in the pulsar magnetosphere. Finally, a phenomenological treatment of wind braking model of pulsars is presented. It can simplify the applications to pulsar braking index, intermittent pulsars and PSR B0540-69.

AI.tldr: The paper examines braking index changes in pulsar PSR B0450-69, linking its evolution to enhanced particle wind causing spin-down state changes and modeling the braking index evolution exponentially. This approach also applies to PSR B0540-69 and intermittent pulsars, enhancing understanding of pulsar braking mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To understand the braking index evolution and spin-down state changes observed in pulsar PSR B0450-69 and to clarify the underlying physics behind these phenomena.
AI.method: The study involves analyzing the spin-down state changes, measuring the braking index over time, proposing that enhanced particle wind causes the state change, modeling the braking index evolution exponentially, and presenting a phenomenological wind braking model.
AI.result: The braking index of PSR B0450-69 exhibits an increasing trend after spin-down state change, consistent with predictions related to particle wind effects. The braking index evolution shows an exponential form, and the braking index for pulsar PSR B0540-69 may reach a steady state. The model simplifies application to pulsar braking indices, intermittent pulsars, and PSR B0540-69.
AI.conclusion: The braking index evolution in PSR B0450-69 is primarily driven by changes in particle wind density, leading to an exponential increase in braking index post spin-down state change. The phenomenological wind braking model effectively explains these observations and provides a framework for future studies and tests of pulsar magnetospheric particle acceleration potentials.

title: Increasing the sensitivity of full-shape galaxy clustering measurements in configuration-space with three-point statistics
summary: We investigate the cosmological constraining power of a compressed line of sight dependent three point correlation function (3PCF) estimator on small scales (<80 Mpc/h) in configuration space, with a particular focus on emission line galaxies (ELGs) targeted by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's Galaxy Redshift Survey (GRS), and complementary luminous red galaxy (LRG) samples observed by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). These scales avoid the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature and are therefore expected to provide information that is largely complementary to standard BAO measurements, while retaining partial overlap with full shape clustering analyses. Our forecasts are based on AbacusSummit simulations at z = 1.1 and z = 0.8, populated with galaxies using halo occupation distribution (HOD) models matched to Roman ELG and DESI LRG samples respectively. The three point measurements are computed with TriCo, a fast configuration space triangle counting code developed for this analysis. After marginalizing over uncertainties in the galaxy halo connection, we find that incorporating the 3PCF yields a substantial improvement over two point statistics alone, tightening the constraint on sigma_8 by a factor of 5 in our fiducial forecast. This gain arises not from a localized feature or specific scale range, but from the cumulative information content across triangle configurations. Restricting to the monopole of the 3PCF captures only part of this information, with the full line of sight dependent measurement providing an additional factor of 2 to 3 improvement over the monopole. Adding line of sight dependent three point information substantially increases the constraining power of small scale configuration space galaxy clustering.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that using the full line of sight dependent 3PCF on small scales (<80 Mpc/h) greatly improves cosmological constraints compared to two-point statistics alone, particularly for ELG and LRG samples from Roman and DESI, with improvements driven by cumulative triangle configuration information across scales.
AI.motivation: To explore the cosmological constraining power of small-scale three point correlation function measurements, particularly for emission line galaxies and luminous red galaxies targeted by upcoming surveys.
AI.method: Used AbacusSummit simulations with halo occupation distribution models matched to Roman ELG and DESI LRG samples at specific redshifts. Computed the 3PCF with a newly developed fast triangle counting code (TriCo), analyzed line of sight dependent 3PCF in configuration space on scales below 80 Mpc/h, and marginalized over galaxy-halo connection uncertainties.
AI.result: Incorporating the 3PCF substantially improves cosmological constraints, tightening sigma_8 by a factor of 5 compared to two-point statistics alone. The full line of sight dependent 3PCF measurement provides an additional 2 to 3 times improvement over the monopole alone. This improvement stems from cumulative information across triangle configurations rather than localized features.
AI.conclusion: Small scale, line of sight dependent three point correlation function measurements provide significant complementary information to traditional two point statistics and BAO analyses, greatly enhancing cosmological parameter constraints for galaxy surveys like Roman and DESI.

title: Accreting stellar-mass black holes
comment: 56 pages, 24 Figures. Submitted to SSRv. Comments welcome
summary: Accreting stellar-mass black holes exhibit dramatic variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, including spectral state transitions, outbursts, and jet production, making them unique laboratories for understanding accretion processes in strong gravitational fields. This review synthesizes recent progress in understanding these systems, focusing on their continuum emission, timing properties, emission lines, and X-ray polarization. A complex interplay between the accretion disk, the so-called corona, and jet underlies the observed spectral and timing behavior, with quasi-periodic oscillations and broadband noise providing windows into the dynamics of the innermost accretion flow. Emission lines across all wavelengths serve as critical diagnostics of disk structure, outflows, and reprocessing, while iron K lines in the X-ray band probe the properties of the inner disk through relativistic reflection. Polarization studies suggest that the corona is likely extended perpendicular to the jet axis in the hard state, while the soft state remains poorly understood, with observations that do not yet conform to simple theoretical expectations; a puzzle that continues to challenge our interpretation of accretion geometry. Despite significant advances, fundamental questions remain about the physical origins of state transitions, the role of magnetic fields in driving outflows and shaping the accretion flow, and the connection between disk instabilities and jet launching. This review underscores the need for future multi-wavelength, timing, and polarimetric studies to deepen our understanding of accretion physics in strong-gravity environments.

AI.tldr: This review synthesizes recent advances in understanding accretion around stellar-mass black holes, focusing on emission, timing, and polarization studies that reveal complex disk-corona-jet interactions, though critical questions about state transitions and magnetic influences remain open.
AI.motivation: To understand the complex accretion processes around stellar-mass black holes exhibiting dramatic variability and to clarify the physics underlying spectral state transitions, outflows, and jet production in strong gravitational fields.
AI.method: A comprehensive review synthesizing recent observational and theoretical progress focusing on continuum emission, timing properties, emission lines, and X-ray polarization studies in accreting stellar-mass black hole systems.
AI.result: Advanced understanding of the interplay between accretion disk, corona, and jet revealed by timing features such as quasi-periodic oscillations and broadband noise; emission lines diagnose disk structure and outflows; X-ray iron K lines probe inner disk; polarization studies indicate an extended corona in hard state. However, fundamental questions about the origins of state transitions, magnetic field roles, and disk-jet connections remain unresolved.
AI.conclusion: The review highlights significant progress but emphasizes persistent challenges in interpreting accretion geometry, particularly in the soft state, and the need for future multi-wavelength, timing, and polarimetric observations to resolve outstanding issues in accretion physics around stellar-mass black holes.

title: Enhancing the Detection Sensitivity of Primordial Parity Violation using Galaxy Spins
summary: It has been recently demonstrated that the signature of primordial parity violation could be imprinted in halo spins, indicating its potential detectability through the late-time galaxy spin field (Shim et al. 2025). In this study, we develop an optimized halo selection strategy to enhance the detection significance of such a signal, focusing on halo mass and local density. Using N-body simulations with parity-asymmetric initial conditions, we show that the optimized halo sample allows for a higher detection sensitivity than the full halo sample, despite its reduced sample size. Finally, we assess the observational feasibility of our strategy and show that future spectroscopic surveys can provide sufficient data to realize this enhanced sensitivity.

AI.tldr: An optimized halo selection method improves the detection of primordial parity violation in halo spins, validated by simulations and feasible with future spectroscopic surveys.
AI.motivation: To improve the detectability of primordial parity violation imprinted in halo spins by optimizing halo selection criteria.
AI.method: Developed an optimized halo selection strategy based on halo mass and local density; employed N-body simulations with parity-asymmetric initial conditions to test detection sensitivity.
AI.result: The optimized halo sample demonstrated higher detection sensitivity to primordial parity violation signals than using the full halo sample, despite involving fewer halos; future spectroscopic surveys are shown to have sufficient data to implement this strategy.
AI.conclusion: Optimized halo selection focusing on mass and local density enhances the detectability of primordial parity violation signals in galaxy spin fields, supporting the feasibility of detecting such signatures with upcoming observational data.

title: Supernova Remnants in the IXPE era: a review
comment: To be published in the Multifrequency Behaviour of High Energy Cosmic Sources - XV Proceedings of Science 2025 issue: https://pos.sissa.it/506/
summary: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has opened a new observational window on the physics of supernova remnants (SNRs) by providing the first spatially resolved X-ray polarimetry measurements. These data directly probe the geometry and turbulence of magnetic fields in regions of efficient particle acceleration, thereby constraining models of diffusive shock acceleration and magnetic-field amplification. IXPE has so far observed six young SNRs (Cas A, Tycho, SN 1006, RX J1713.7-3946, Vela Jr., and RCW 86) with published results on the first five. The observations reveal significant polarization in all cases, with degrees of polarization ranging from 5% to over 30%, reflecting different turbulence levels and environmental conditions. Three remnants (Cas A, Tycho, and SN 1006) show predominantly radial magnetic fields, while RX J1713.7-3946 and Vela Jr. display tangential morphologies. This dual behavior, not simply correlated with evolutionary stage, challenges the long-standing dichotomy inferred from radio observations and suggests that both shock velocity and circumstellar medium density play key roles in shaping magnetic-field topology. IXPE's results mark a major step toward disentangling the processes governing cosmic-ray acceleration in young SNR shocks, with ongoing and future observations expected to further constrain the interplay between turbulence, shock dynamics, and particle acceleration.

AI.tldr: IXPE's spatially resolved X-ray polarimetry of young supernova remnants reveals varying magnetic field geometries that challenge previous models, improving insight into particle acceleration mechanisms at SNR shocks.
AI.motivation: To enhance understanding of magnetic-field configurations and turbulence in young SNRs, which are critical for models of diffusive shock acceleration and magnetic-field amplification associated with cosmic-ray acceleration.
AI.method: IXPE performed spatially resolved X-ray polarimetry on six young supernova remnants, measuring the degree and morphology of polarization to probe magnetic field geometry and turbulence.
AI.result: Significant polarization degrees of 5% to over 30% were detected across all observed SNRs, with distinct radial or tangential magnetic field morphologies depending on individual environmental conditions and shock parameters.
AI.conclusion: IXPE observations have revealed significant and diverse X-ray polarization in young SNRs, indicating complex magnetic field geometries influenced by shock velocity and circumstellar medium density, thereby challenging previous interpretations based solely on radio data.

title: The stability of voids in the local Universe: the role of the cosmological constant
summary: The Vlasov kinetic formalism is employed to study the evolution and stability of cosmic voids in the local Universe, taking into account not only gravitational attraction but also the repulsive effect of the cosmological constant (local dark energy). In accordance with the theorem on the general function for the identity between the gravitational fields of a sphere and a point mass, the cosmological constant provides a natural explanation for the Hubble tension as arising due to local and global flows characterized by different Hubble parameters. The crucial role of the Λ-repulsion in maintaining the stability of voids at the present epoch is demonstrated when Landau damping suppresses discrete collapse modes and prevents random local density perturbations inside the voids from growing and involving new galaxies to the walls. Inside the voids, the Λ-repulsion exceeds the attractive force of the residual matter, driving matter outward and accelerating its migration toward the void boundaries. In the local (late) Universe, cosmic voids have entered a stage characterized by stable and more pronounced walls, as can be studied by observational surveys across different redshift ranges.

AI.tldr: This paper uses kinetic theory to show that the cosmological constant's repulsive force stabilizes cosmic voids by preventing collapse and driving matter outward, explaining the Hubble tension and the observed void wall structures in the local Universe.
AI.motivation: To understand the evolution and stability of cosmic voids in the local Universe considering both gravitational attraction and the cosmological constant's repulsive effect.
AI.method: Application of the Vlasov kinetic formalism to model cosmic void dynamics, incorporating gravitational and cosmological constant effects, and analyzing Landau damping to suppress collapse modes.
AI.result: Demonstrated that the cosmological constant's repulsive effect is crucial for the stability of cosmic voids by overcoming matter attraction, driving matter outward, supporting stable void walls, and explaining the Hubble tension due to different local and global flows.
AI.conclusion: The Λ-repulsion from the cosmological constant plays a vital role in maintaining cosmic void stability and structure in the local Universe, reconciling observational phenomena such as the Hubble tension and the pronounced formation of void walls.

title: A Whisper from Within: Response of a Pulsar Timing Array to an Internal Gravitational-wave Source
summary: Millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are abundant in globular clusters (GCs) and probably also in galactic nuclei. They offer the potential to form a miniature pulsar timing array (mini-PTA) to detect nanohertz gravitational-wave (GW) sources located inside the array. Since the size of such an array is comparable to the wavelength of GW, the conventional plane-wave approximation becomes invalid, and near-field effects, including wavefront curvature, non-radiative self-field of the GW source, and direct perturbation of pulsar by GW, become significant. In this work, we incorporate these effects in a comprehensive model to calculate the timing residual induced by a GW source inside a mini-PTA. We also consider realistic GW source configurations in GCs (M15 and $ω$ Centauri) and in galactic nuclei (Sgr A* and M31), and find that for MSPs located sufficiently close to the GW source (within a few wavelengths), the residual can reach $1~μ\mathrm{s}$ in GCs and up to milliseconds in galactic centers, within the potential detection reach of current radio telescopes. Crucially, when the pulsar lies within a few GW wavelengths of the source, the non-radiative field dominates and causes the residual to rise much more steeply (between $1/r_e^2$ and $1/r_e^4$, where $r_e$ is the distance to the source) than the conventional far-field scaling ($1/r_e$). These results demonstrate that mini-PTAs in GCs or galactic nuclei can serve as powerful probes of otherwise invisible GW sources, including intermediate-mass and supermassive black hole binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper models near-field gravitational wave effects on millisecond pulsar timing arrays in globular clusters and galactic nuclei, showing enhanced timing residuals near sources that enable detecting intermediate and supermassive black hole binaries using current telescopes.
AI.motivation: Millisecond pulsars in globular clusters and galactic nuclei can form miniature pulsar timing arrays to detect gravitational waves, but near-field effects invalidate conventional approximations, necessitating a comprehensive model.
AI.method: Developed a model including near-field effects like wavefront curvature, non-radiative self-field, and direct GW perturbations on pulsars; applied it to realistic gravitational wave sources in specific globular clusters and galactic nuclei.
AI.result: Found that timing residuals can reach microsecond to millisecond levels for pulsars close to GW sources, with non-radiative fields dominating at short distances and causing steeper residual increases than traditional far-field models predict, making detection feasible with current radio telescopes.
AI.conclusion: Miniature pulsar timing arrays in globular clusters and galactic nuclei can effectively detect and probe gravitational wave sources, including intermediate-mass and supermassive black hole binaries, by leveraging near-field effects absent in conventional far-field approximations.

title: Is dark matter decaying ?
summary: An enduring signature of the decay of unstable dark matter constituents into other particles would manifest as a measurable discrepancy in the matter density parameter (Omega_m) between the recombination era (z ~ 1000) and the local Universe (z = 0). While precision measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background tightly constrain the initial matter budget, evaluating this decay hypothesis requires an equally precise audit of the current epoch. We find that current local inventories of baryonic and dark matter are subject to systematic uncertainties - particularly in accounting for the warm-hot intergalactic medium, diffuse intra-cluster media, and the exact profiles of low-mass dark matter halos - rendering a definitive verdict on late-time dark matter decay currently hard to pin down. Furthermore, existing astrophysical bounds on cosmic rays, the diffuse gamma-ray background, and reionization history already heavily constrain potential decay channels during this epoch. However, next-generation observational technology is poised to resolve these local accounting gaps. Upcoming high-resolution spectroscopic surveys, next-decade X-ray missions, and advanced weak lensing campaigns will drastically reduce baryon and mass-mapping uncertainties, transforming the late-time matter audit into a cleaner, more definitive test.

AI.tldr: Testing unstable dark matter decay via discrepancies in matter density between early and late Universe is currently limited by uncertainties in local matter inventories and existing constraints. Future observational improvements promise more definitive assessments.
AI.motivation: Investigate potential signatures of unstable dark matter decay by comparing matter density parameters at recombination and the local Universe epochs.
AI.method: Analyze current local inventories of baryonic and dark matter and assess systematic uncertainties in various cosmic components; review existing astrophysical constraints on decay channels; discuss prospects with upcoming observational technologies.
AI.result: Current local measurements of matter density have significant uncertainties, hindering a conclusive test of late-time dark matter decay. Astrophysical constraints already limit many decay scenarios, but future high-resolution surveys and missions will significantly improve matter accounting precision.
AI.conclusion: Although current data cannot definitively confirm or rule out late-time unstable dark matter decay due to systematic uncertainties, forthcoming observational advancements will enable more precise tests and potentially resolve this question.

title: A FAST search for radio pulsations during the dormant state of the AMSPs IGR J00291+5934 and MAXI J1957+032
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures; accepted for publication by A&A
summary: Accreting millisecond pulsars (AMSPs) and transitional millisecond pulsars (tMSPs) are neutron star low-mass X-ray binaries which can evolve into "recycled" radio millisecond pulsars. In both types of systems, X-ray pulsations have been detected during phases of X-ray activity when matter accretion through a disc is turned on. On the other hand, when accretion stops, and these systems enter the quiescent, low-luminosity X-ray state, only tMSPs become visible as radio pulsars. Despite several attempts, radio pulsations have never been detected in quiescent AMSPs, except for IGR J18245$-$2452. In this manuscript, we present the results of two observational campaigns performed on the AMSPs IGR J00291+5934 and MAXI J1957+032 with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope ($\it{FAST}$) in L-band (1-1.5 GHz). Both sources have most likely been observed in quiescence, as suggested by the upper limits on their X-ray and optical flux obtained with Swift and the Las Cumbres Observatory, respectively. We have performed a deep search for coherent periodicities in radio but found no significant candidate signal, either at the known spin frequency of those sources or at other frequencies. Assuming a pulse duty cycle of 10%, we derive upper limits on the pulsed radio flux density of 3.3 $μ$Jy and 5.6 $μ$Jy for IGR J00291+5934 and MAXI J1957+032, respectively, which are the most stringent limits so far for any known persistent AMSP.

AI.tldr: The study used FAST to search for radio pulsations in two quiescent accreting millisecond pulsars but found none, setting the most stringent upper limits on radio flux and highlighting differences in emission compared to transitional millisecond pulsars.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence of radio pulsations in quiescent accreting millisecond pulsars (AMSPs), a phenomenon detected only in transitional MSPs (tMSPs) during quiescence but rarely in AMSPs, in order to understand their emission properties and evolutionary connection to recycled radio millisecond pulsars.
AI.method: Two observational campaigns using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) in L-band (1-1.5 GHz) targeting AMSPs IGR J00291+5934 and MAXI J1957+032, combined with upper limits on their X-ray and optical flux from Swift and the Las Cumbres Observatory, to conduct a deep search for coherent radio pulsations during their quiescent states.
AI.result: No significant coherent radio pulsations were detected at the known spin frequencies or elsewhere for both sources, leading to the derivation of the most stringent upper limits on pulsed radio flux densities for persistent AMSPs, namely 3.3 μJy for IGR J00291+5934 and 5.6 μJy for MAXI J1957+032, assuming a 10% pulse duty cycle.
AI.conclusion: Despite deep radio observations with FAST during quiescence, radio pulsations remain undetected in the AMSPs studied, suggesting a fundamental difference in radio emission behavior between persistent AMSPs and tMSPs in their low-luminosity states; these constraints provide valuable input for models of neutron star evolution and pulsar emission mechanisms.

title: Finite-Core Signatures in LISA-Band Wave-Optics Lensing by Low-Mass Dark Matter Halos
summary: LISA-band gravitational waves from massive binary black holes can be diffractively lensed by low-mass dark matter halos and subhalos, so their frequency-dependent amplification can probe the inner density profile. We isolate the generic finite-core part of this signal by comparing fixed-mass Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) and cored-NFW lenses and propagating both profiles to the complex wave-optics amplification factor. A finite core smooths the time-delay response and reshapes the diffraction peak; an NFW template with a lower concentration can mimic part of the effect, but structured complex residuals remain after time and phase alignment. The residual peaks for intermediate cores, $r_c/r_s\simeq0.25$--$0.3$. An SIDM-inspired isothermal-core profile gives the same qualitative response, showing that the signal is not an artifact of one cored parameterization. For a fiducial LISA source, an appreciable mismatch requires favorable near alignment and $M_{\rm vir}\gtrsim 10^7M_\odot$. The result is a finite-core baseline for isolated line-of-sight halos and for subhalos perturbing strongly lensed macro-images.

AI.tldr: This study shows that finite cores in dark matter halos affect diffractive lensing of LISA gravitational waves, enabling probes of inner halo density profiles through characteristic frequency-dependent amplification features.
AI.motivation: To utilize gravitational wave signals from massive binary black holes detected by LISA to probe the inner density profiles of low-mass dark matter halos and subhalos via diffractive lensing effects.
AI.method: Comparison of fixed-mass Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) and cored-NFW lens models, propagating their profiles through to the complex wave-optics amplification factor to isolate effects of finite cores on frequency-dependent amplification.
AI.result: A finite core in the lens smooths the time-delay response and alters diffraction peaks; while NFW templates with lower concentration mimic some effects, complex residuals remain after alignment. Similar qualitative responses arise from isothermal-core profiles inspired by self-interacting dark matter, indicating robustness. Significant mismatch occurs under near alignment and halo virial masses above 10^7 solar masses for LISA sources.
AI.conclusion: Finite-core density profiles in low-mass dark matter halos produce distinctive diffractive lensing signatures in LISA-band gravitational waves, offering a baseline for identifying and characterizing isolated line-of-sight halos and subhalos in strongly lensed systems.

title: On the impact of the carbon fusion rate over the properties of superbursts -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA
summary: Context: Superbursts are very energetic explosions in the crust of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). These are triggered by unstable carbon burning at $T\leq 10^{9}$ K. In recent years, there has been a re-examination of the carbon fusion rate, finding that at these temperatures it might be either smaller or higher with respect to the classic rate from Caughler \& Fowler (1988) by a factor $10^{3}$. Aims: We explore the consequences changing the carbon fusion rate has over the physics of superbursts. Methods: For simulating superbursts, we employ the public code MESA v.24.08.1, as well as four versions of the carbon fusion reaction rate. Results: An enhancement of the reaction rate by a factor $10^{3}$ at $T\leq 10^9$~K reduces the recurrence and decay times of the superburst, as well as the column depth at ignition. The opposite behavior is observed when the carbon fusion rate is reduced by the same factor. The maximum temperature reached during the explosion is also sensitive to these changes, leading to either an enhancement or a reduction in the synthesis of $α$-nuclides. These changes are comparable to the effect of reducing the amount of base heating at the bottom of the envelope.

AI.tldr: Changing the carbon fusion rate by a factor of 10^3 affects superburst recurrence, decay, ignition depth, peak temperature, and nucleosynthesis, highlighting the importance of precise rate measurements for modeling neutron star superbursts.
AI.motivation: There is uncertainty in the carbon fusion rate at low temperatures (around 10^9 K), which affects the understanding of superbursts in neutron stars. This paper aims to explore how variations in this rate impact superburst physics.
AI.method: Superbursts are simulated using the MESA code with four different versions of the carbon fusion reaction rate to assess the impact of rate changes on superburst properties.
